target_customer: Spine surgeons and interventional radiologists, bought by hospitals
problem: Traditional surgical navigation is costly, slow to set up and takes the surgeon's eyes off the patient; Skylight projects anatomy onto the patient.
business_model: Medical device capital equipment (pre-commercial, not FDA cleared per site)

founders.name: Eldrick Millares
prior_employers: Lidar startup (led hardware and software teams)
education: Stanford, BS and MS in electrical engineering

founders.name: James Hu
founders.background_notes: Source: YC page describes him as MD, bioengineer and medical device builder; met Millares as Stanford freshman dormmates

competitors.name: Augmedics (xvision Spine System)
competitors.what: AR headset giving surgeons 3D anatomy views in spine surgery
competitors.traction_then: FDA cleared in 2019 per a trade report

technical_complexity.rationale: Real-time projection with sub-millimeter patient tracking in an operating room, plus regulatory clearance.

defensibility.rationale: Tracking method and FDA clearance path create barriers, but large medtech players can acquire or copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not documented; no clearance for Illuminant as of 2026 per its site.

market_need_then: Spine navigation is an established category with large vendors; the company argues existing systems are costly and disruptive to workflow.

identity.voice_and_tone: Ambitious and visionary; x-ray vision, superpowers

branding.brand_signature: Skylight product and A NEW WAY OF SEEING
branding.community_and_virality: Fortune and trade press covered the 2026 round, mostly the technology.

brand_strength.rationale: Evocative name matching the projection idea; brand coverage is mainly about the product.

outcome_analysis: Illuminant Surgical is active and raised an $8.4M seed in April 2026, about half of it federal grants per Fortune, nearly four years after the S22 batch. That slow capital path is typical for device companies, where clearance and clinical validation come before sales. Its main risks are regulatory timing and well-resourced navigation incumbents.
notes: Seed cross-checked by Fortune and AuntMinnie (both reached via search results, not opened). Grant share conflicts: Fortune says roughly half, Pulse says about $4.2M. Earlier grants (NSF, NCI, NIA) are mentioned but amounts and dates not found, hence partial coverage. Augmedics is dated 2019 by a trade report, before the batch. Founder education for Hu not found.
